subject: Doubt about lognormal model in INLA

messages.author: 6fb9d7eb23edd043
messages.subject: Doubt about lognormal model in INLA
parts:
Dear INLA community

I am working in a problem where I am interested in having only positive values in the support of the answer variable. I was initially working with the Guassian model trying to control the support with the use of prior but those prior ended being too informative which is something I do not want in this case. So the next option was to use a lognormal model but it is not clear for me if INLA takes the log of only the answer, only of the covariables or both. I mean this

Option 1:

log(y)~Beta_0+x1+x2

Option 2:

y ~ Beta_0 + log(x1) + log(x2)

Option 3:

log(y)~Beta_0+log(x1)+log(x2)

I am interested to return the log transformation to have the data in the original scale having also the benefit of all being positive, and the best case would be option 1, that would be 

exp(model$summary$fitted.values)
 
Right? Or does INLA make any other process with the lognormal model that needs to be known to have the data in the original scale or to work with the lognormal model in general?

Thank you
